question: A 16-year-old girl has restricted her food intake severely over 8 months, with a BMI of 15.2 kg/m² (well below normal for age), intense fear of gaining weight, and body image distortion. She denies binge-purge behaviour. Which DSM-5 diagnosis best fits?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Bulimia Nervosa in DSM-5 is characterised by recurrent binge-purge cycles, NOT restriction alone. DSM-5 does not recognise a 'restricting type' of bulimia.

Correct. DSM-5 Criterion A = restriction leading to significantly low body weight; Criterion B = intense fear of gaining weight; Criterion C = disturbance in self-perceived weight/shape. No binge-purge behaviour = restricting subtype. Both subtypes require all three criteria.

ARFID involves food restriction without the fear of weight gain or body image disturbance that are required for AN. This patient's intense fear of gaining weight and body image distortion point to AN.
OSFED is used when full criteria for a named disorder are NOT met. This patient meets all three DSM-5 criteria for AN restricting type.

overallFeedback.feedback: Revisit DSM-5 criteria. Anorexia Nervosa requires all three: (A) significantly low body weight due to restriction, (B) intense fear of weight gain, (C) disturbance in self-perceived weight or shape. Subtypes = restricting vs binge-purge. This case has no binge-purge, so it is AN restricting type.

Correct. Anorexia Nervosa restricting type (DSM-5) = three criteria: significant low weight + fear of weight gain + body-image disturbance, WITHOUT recurrent binge-purge episodes. Remember: AN carries the highest mortality of any psychiatric disorder.
